title: Build a Better Data Center
summary: Create a community-aware hypothetical design that explains its technical choices and tradeoffs.
objectives: Integrate technical systems and community constraints in a design.
Document a decision, accepted tradeoff, remaining risk, and possible improvement.

vocab.def: A person or group affected by a decision or interested in its outcome.
How much work, information, or resource a system can handle.
A choice that gains something while giving up or risking something else.

sections.heading: Your design brief
sections.body: Design a hypothetical data center for a community. Include a site, computing needs, power, cooling, networking, security, reliability, sustainability, workforce roles, and community considerations.

sections.heading: Keep a decision log
sections.body: For each major choice, explain what you chose, why, what tradeoff you accepted, what risk remains, and what you would improve with more evidence or resources.

sections.heading: Show more than one perspective
sections.body: Include at least one possible benefit and one community concern. Your design may seem helpful, need stronger safeguards, need to change, or need more information. The rubric rewards reasoning, not a predetermined conclusion.

practice.prompt: Before presenting, check that your design includes every required system and a decision log for site, reliability, sustainability, and community impact.

project.title: Build a Better Data Center
submissionOptions: written design brief with a labeled systems diagram
accessible digital outline or slide-style design
physical or digital model with an oral explanation
rubric: communicates clearly and reflects on remaining risk

quiz.question: What makes a design decision strong?
options: It explains needs, evidence, tradeoffs, risks, and possible improvement
It chooses the biggest system without constraints
It promises that no problem can occur
quiz.answer: It explains needs, evidence, tradeoffs, risks, and possible improvement

levels: Developing: connects a choice to one constraint or system
Proficient: explains integrated systems, evidence, tradeoffs, community perspectives, and remaining risk

reflectionPrompt: What was your hardest design decision, and what would you investigate before improving it?
